title: Bounded provider-neutral typed relation algebra
independentExamples: A fully renamed two-edge algebra composes nonce relation classes and returns a typed proof witness.
A renamed inverse query reverses declared relation semantics without depending on source vocabulary.
A meaning-changing relation order produces a different semantic class, while missing refinement evidence remains ambiguous.
outputTypes: SOLVED with semantic values and ordered witness
UNKNOWN, INCONSISTENT_CONTEXT, NO_APPLICABLE_METHOD, RESOURCE_LIMIT, or UNPARSED
preconditions: The task and algebra identifiers and record shapes validate.
Relation values, inverse classes, and composition classes are declared by trusted package projection.
The source adapter validates and bounds all structured evidence before method execution.
invariants: Core control flow depends only on semantic types, declared relation metadata, features, and resource policy.
Entity names, source rows, expected answers, benchmark identity, and case order do not select an answer.
Every solved result retains an ordered edge witness and composition tree.
Missing refinement evidence returns AMBIGUOUS rather than choosing a source label.
All bounded binary parenthesizations are considered; relation order remains semantically significant.
uncertaintySemantics: Missing distinguishing features produce AMBIGUOUS; disconnected evidence produces UNKNOWN; conflicting features or incompatible shortest paths produce INCONSISTENT_CONTEXT; exhausted policy produces RESOURCE_LIMIT.
proofBehavior: A solved result records asserted or inverse edge direction, fact identifiers, semantic classes, path length, explored states, and a binary composition proof. Ambiguity retains alternative values and witnesses.
kbMigration: No generic package-schema migration is required. Relation semantics remain declarative in independently versioned typed-relation-algebra constraints.
